quotes: “ Uncle , you are not looking well to-night . ”
“ I 'm not well , Florence . I sometimes doubt if I shall ever be any better . ”
“ Surely , uncle , you cannot mean —— ”
“ Yes , my child , I have reason to believe that I am nearing the end . ”
“ I cannot bear to hear you speak so , uncle , ”
“ You are not an old man . You are but fifty-four . ”
“ True , Florence , but it is not years only that make a man old . Two great sorrows have embittered my life . First , the death of my dearly beloved wife , and next , the loss of my boy , Harvey . ”
“ It is long since I have heard you refer to my cousin 's loss . I thought you had become reconciled — no , I do not mean that ,— I thought your regret might be less poignant . ”
“ I have not permitted myself to speak of it , but I have never ceased to think of it day and night . ”

“ If he had died , I might , as you say , have become reconciled ; but he was abducted at the age of four by a revengeful servant whom I had discharged from my employment . Heaven knows whether he is living or dead , but it is impressed upon my mind that he still lives , it may be in misery , it may be as a criminal , while I , his unhappy father , live on in luxury which I cannot enjoy , with no one to care for me —— ”
“ Do n't say that , uncle , ”
“ You know that I love you , Uncle John . ”
“ And I , too , uncle . ”
“ Yes , ”
“ I must not forget that I have a nephew and a niece . You are both dear to me , but no one can take the place of the boy I have lost . ”
“ But it is so long ago , uncle , ”
“ It must be fourteen years . ”
“ It is fourteen years . ”
“ And the boy is long since dead ! ”
“ No , no ! ”
“ I do not , I will not , believe it . He still lives , and I live only in the hope of one day clasping him in my arms . ”
“ That is very improbable , uncle , ”
“ There is n't one chance in a hundred that my cousin still lives . The grave has closed over him long since . The sooner you make up your mind to accept the inevitable the better . ”
“ How can you speak so , Curtis ? ”
“ Leave Uncle John the hope that he has so long cherished . I have a presentiment that Harvey still lives . ”
“ You , too , believe it possible , Florence ? ”
“ Yes , uncle . I not only believe it possible , but probable . How old would Harvey be if he still lived ? ”
“ Eighteen — nearly a year older than yourself . ”
“ How strange ! I always think of him as a little boy . ”
“ And I , too , Florence . He rises before me in his little velvet suit , as he was when I last saw him , with his sweet , boyish face , in which his mother 's looks were reflected . ”
“ Yet , if still living , ”
“ he is a rough street boy , perchance serving his time at Blackwell 's Island , and , a hardened young ruffian , whom it would be bitter mortification to recognize as your son . ”
“ That 's the sorrowful part of it , ”
“ That is what I most dread . ”
“ Then , since even if he were living you would not care to recognize him , why not cease to think of him , or else regard him as dead ? ”
“ Curtis Waring , have you no heart ? ”
“ Indeed , Florence , you ought to know , ”
“ I know nothing of it , ”
“ You know that the dearest wish of my heart is to find favor in your eyes . Uncle , you know my wish , and approve of it , do you not ? ”
“ Yes , Curtis ; you and Florence are equally dear to me , and it is my hope that you may be united . In that case , there will be no division of my fortune . It will be left to you jointly . ”
“ Believe me , sir , ”
“ believe me , that I fully appreciate your goodness . I am sure Florence joins with me —— ”
“ Florence can speak for herself , ”
“ My uncle needs no assurance from me . He is always kind , and I am always grateful . ”
“ I do not doubt your affection , ”
“ and I have shown it by making you my joint heirs in the event of your marriage ; but it is only fair to say that my property goes to my boy , if he still lives . ”
“ But , sir , ”
“ is not that likely to create unnecessary trouble ? It can never be known , and meanwhile —— ”
“ You and Florence will hold the property in trust . ”
“ Have you so specified in your will ? ”

“ I have made two wills . Both are in yonder secretary . By the first the property is bequeathed to you and Florence . By the second and later , it goes to my lost boy in the event of his recovery . Of course , you and Florence are not forgotten , but the bulk of the property goes to Harvey . ”
“ I sincerely wish the boy might be restored to you , ”

“ Believe me , the loss of the property would affect me little , if you could be made happy by realizing your warmest desire ; but , uncle , I think it only the part of a friend to point out to you , as I have already done , the baselessness of any such expectation . ”
“ It may be as you say , Curtis , ”
“ If I were thoroughly convinced of it , I would destroy the later will , and leave my property absolutely to you and Florence . ”
“ No , uncle , ”
“ make no change ; let the will stand . ”
“ Is the girl mad ? ”
“ Must she forever balk me ? ”
“ Let it be so for the present , then , ”
“ Curtis , will you ring the bell ? I am tired , and shall retire to my couch early . ”
“ Let me help you , Uncle John , ”
“ It is too much for your strength , my child . I am growing more and more helpless . ”
“ I , too , can help , ”
“ Florence , ”
“ and let us talk this matter over . ”
“ As you please , ”
“ Will you be seated ? ”
“ No ; our interview will be brief . ”
“ Then I will come to the point . Uncle John wishes to see us united . ”
“ It can never be ! ”
“ You profess to love Uncle John , and yet you would disappoint his cherished hope ! ”
“ Is it his cherished hope ? ”
“ There is no doubt about it . He has spoken to me more than once on the subject . Feeling that his end is near , he wishes to leave you in charge of a protector . ”
